convergence_checkpoint.severity: disclosed, non-blocking -- does not contradict ADR-0146's own text and does not prevent honest closure
convergence_checkpoint.finding: A full POSITIVE composed-tape fixture (a custom source_roster.json + raw-event members) cannot be carried through the FIXED/legacy authority's own action-execution-admission chain (_complete_signed_graph/_graph_live, the construction tests/pipeline/test_captured_authorization.py's existing ADR-0129 tests use).
convergence_checkpoint.root_cause: _p4_close_admission's _p4_terminal_parent_projection (trust.py) re-signs the captured root's own member_manifest_sha256 into the 'root-publication-receipt' evidence it verifies, then checks the resulting projection digest against trust.py's HARDCODED, two-entry _P4_APPROVED_ROOT_PROJECTIONS allowlist (trust.py:3861). Confirmed empirically: driving a custom member set (even with the admission graph's own signing pass using the SAME custom content) through _complete_signed_graph/_graph_live raises ValueError('fixed external root policy projection refused') at commit_p4_batch -> close_admission time, because the resulting projection digest is not one of the two pre-baked digests that already-existing default fixtures (f4._publish's and f4._foreign_publish's own unmodified content) produce.
convergence_checkpoint.why_not_fixable_within_scope: The only fix would be adding a third entry to trust.py's _P4_APPROVED_ROOT_PROJECTIONS tuple (or otherwise editing trust.py's admission-verification code) -- forbidden outright by ADR-0146 Decision point 10 ('No trust.py edit, and no trust.py import... No correction to _validate_capture_request, commit_legacy_capture, or commit_p4_batch is proposed or required' -- Decision point 1). This is the fixed corpus's own intentional design (a genuinely FIXED, pre-approved external policy grant, as opposed to the dynamic authority's fresh per-test graph via ADR-0141/0142/0143) -- not a test-construction mistake discovered late; it was found, diagnosed, and worked around within this same RED cycle before any GREEN code was written.
convergence_checkpoint.why_not_a_blocker: ADR-0146 Decision point 8's own text explicitly anticipates and permits exactly this asymmetry: 'A fixed-authority case may additionally exist (e.g., as a second comparison case or a regression guard) but does not substitute for the dynamic-authority case this point requires.' The ADR's own MANDATORY positive proof is the dynamic-authority case (row 2), which is fully achieved and genuinely passes. Every other matrix row needing custom fixture content is driven through the dynamic authority instead of the fixed one (compose_replay_tape's own validation/round-trip/causal-order logic is independent of which authority supplied record/session/published -- this is itself part of what row 2 verifies, per ADR Context point 1's 'resolver-type-agnostic by construction' claim). Row 1 is implemented instead as a fixed-authority accessor-reachability/regression case: a real read_member_bytes call against real committed FIXED-authority content (the default, unmodified fixture), correctly refused by compose_replay_tape's own roster shape-check rather than silently accepted -- a genuine behavioral exercise of the fixed path, matching Decision point 8's own 'regression guard' framing.
